subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - post-call recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - post-call recap

Hi Sam / Olivia -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the agreed next steps so we have a clear PoC path for validating end-to-end p95/p99 latency:

Call highlights:
- Goal: quantify end-to-end p95 and p99 for FinLytics chat flows and compare Redwood hosted API vs your current provider.
- Primary SLOs discussed: p95 and p99 end-to-end latency (user request -> UI receives final token).
- Additional constraints: throughput profile (QPS), peak concurrency, average payload size, and streaming/partial-result semantics.

Action items (Redwood):
1) Share our latency measurement deck and SLO measurement template (attached).
2) Provide an initial estimate for hosted API p95/p99 with FinLytics' workload profile.
3) Propose PoC plan: synthetic load + shadow traffic sampling + 2-week live test window.

Action items (FinLytics):
- Share sample payloads and typical concurrency/traffic shape (peak and baseline).
- Confirm whether the product relies on streaming partial tokens (we heard yes for chat UX).

Notes on measurement scope:
- By default our hosted API measurements are end-to-end to the Redwood edge (includes our runtime, queuing, and the network up to our edge). We'll call that out explicitly in the template so we can align on whether you want to include your internal network to the client.
- For streaming flows we'll capture first-byte latency and final completion latency (both p95/p99) and show differences versus non-streamed completions.

Attachments: redwood_latency-deck.pdf, slo_measurement_template.xlsx (blank) - please fill sample_payloads.json if you can.

Next proposed step: assuming you can share sample payloads, we can schedule a 30-min kick-off next week to lock the PoC scope and timeline. What days work for your engineering lead?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - post-call recap

Thanks Laura - useful summary. A few clarifications from our side so the PoC aligns with how we measure today:

- Current provider end-to-end (what our telemetry reports): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~980ms for chat completions (these numbers include provider-side batching and their edge-to-client hops; they do not include our internal frontend overhead).
- Streaming: yes, we stream partial tokens for the chat UI. First-token latency is critical for perceived responsiveness.
- Traffic shape: peak concurrency ~400 active users (peak trading hours), average concurrency ~120, sustained QPS during peak ~110 QPS for the chat endpoint.
- Payloads: typical prompt + context is ~1.2KB (we will attach a few sanitized examples).

Questions:
1) When you say 'end-to-end to the Redwood edge', does that include the TLS handshake + network RTT to your edge from our EC2 region, or only your runtime processing time? We need to be careful comparing apples-to-apples.
2) For streaming first-byte latency, do you measure first-byte at p95 for the entire request (i.e., cumulative across queueing + compute + edge), or do you separate queueing vs runtime?
3) Will your hosted numbers include your standard batching heuristics, or will the PoC lock batching off to match our current provider's settings?

We'll attach sample_payloads.json in a follow-up email; can you also populate the template with the fields you need from our side so we don't miss anything?

Thanks,
Sam Torres
Senior Product Manager - Chat
FinLytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - post-call recap

Sam - thanks for the detail, very helpful. Answers inline below and a proposed PoC approach.

1) 'End-to-end to the Redwood edge' scope:
- Our hosted default measurement includes client -> Redwood edge network RTT (TLS + network) + edge ingress processing + runtime queueing + inference execution + edge egress to our response handoff. We explicitly call out the network region in the measurement sheet so we can subtract client-side network if you want to normalize to your internal metrics.

2) Streaming first-byte measurement:
- We capture first-byte (initial partial token) p95/p99 as a separate metric and also report completion p95/p99. We break out queueing vs runtime where possible (queue wait time vs actual token generation time) in the PoC reports.

3) Batching behavior:
- For the hosted API we will run with standard batching turned on (intelligent batching based on request shape and latency SLO). For a direct apples-to-apples comparison we can run a variant with batching limited or disabled - we'll surface both numbers.

Preliminary guidance (based on similar customers and your profile):
- For payloads ~1.2KB and concurrency shape you shared, our hosted API typically hits ~350ms p95 and ~800ms p99 for completion latency (non-streamed) under standard batching and prefix caching assumptions. Streaming first-byte p95 is often <120ms. These are preliminary estimates - PoC will validate.

Proposed PoC steps:
A) You provide sample_payloads.json and confirm region(s) to test from (we assume us-west-2).
B) Redwood runs synthetic sweep across concurrency points + a shadowed production run for 48-72 hours to capture realistic variance.
C) Deliverable: side-by-side p95/p99 reports (first-byte and completion), throughput charts, and configuration notes (batching, cache hits, concurrency).

I attached a filled example of the measurement template and a sample latency deck for the SLA conversation. Can you confirm your engineering lead's availability next Tue/Wed for a 30-min PoC kick-off?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
